title: Vault
description: HashiCorp Vault (standalone, file storage, Kubernetes auth for External Secrets). Curated: no official HashiCorp dashboard exists; panels follow the vault-mixin (adinhodovic) and the HashiCorp telemetry reference, minus HA/Raft/replication/audit panels that cannot have data here. Source list: docs/dashboards/security.md

list.name: Vault sealed
list.textFormat: vault_core_unsealed = 0 on {{instance}}: secrets cannot be read

panels.description: How to read this dashboard.

options.content:
### Vault: the lab's only secret store
**What it does here.** `vault/vault-0` (standalone, `file` storage on a `local-path` volume) holds every credential under
`secret/homelab/*`. External Secrets logs in with Kubernetes auth (role `external-secrets`) and copies the values into
Kubernetes Secrets. Nobody else talks to Vault day to day.

**The #1 risk: sealed.** Vault starts **sealed** after every restart of `vault-0` (node reboot included). While sealed,
existing Kubernetes Secrets keep working, but nothing refreshes and new ExternalSecrets stay pending. Alert `VaultSealed`
fires after 5 min; the CronJob `vault-autounseal` unseals within 5 min (`docs/runbooks/vault.md`).

**Healthy looks like:** *Seal status* = UNSEALED, *Active node* = 1, scrape UP, success rate 100 %, a few requests per
minute (ESO logins and reads every refresh), no irrevocable leases.

**When something is red:** sealed → `kubectl --context k8s01 -n vault create job --from=cronjob/vault-autounseal unseal-now`
or `scripts/vault.sh unseal`. Scrape DOWN → is `vault-0` running (`kubectl --context k8s01 -n vault get pod`)?
5xx responses → `kubectl --context k8s01 -n vault logs vault-0`. Then check the *External Secrets* dashboard.

Request/token/lease panels need `prometheus_retention_time = "24h"` (set in `helm-charts/vault`, active after the next
`vault-0` restart); with the old 30s value they are mostly empty. Docs: [telemetry](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics), [vault-mixin](https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin).

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

panels.title: Seal status
panels.description: vault_core_unsealed: 1 when Vault is unsealed, 0 when sealed. Sealed = Vault answers but serves no secrets; External Secrets cannot refresh. Normal: UNSEALED. Red: run the auto-unseal Job or scripts/vault.sh unseal. Same expression as the lab alert VaultSealed (vault-raw) and the vault-mixin alert. Source: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics

panels.title: Metrics scrape
panels.description: up for job vault-internal (ServiceMonitor, /v1/sys/metrics every 60s). Vault serves metrics even while sealed, so DOWN means the pod or the Service is gone. Lab alert VaultDown fires after 10 min without a successful scrape. Source: Prometheus up metric.

panels.title: Active node
panels.description: vault_core_active: 1 when this node is the active node. A standalone Vault must be active (the vault-mixin alert VaultNoActiveNode fires when the sum is < 1 for 5m). 0 while sealed or starting. Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Up since
panels.description: Time since the Vault process started (process_start_time_seconds). Every start means Vault was sealed until it was unsealed again: a recent start explains a VaultSealed alert. Source: Go client process collector.

panels.title: Auto-unseal CronJob: last success
panels.description: Age of the last successful run of CronJob vault-autounseal (kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time). It runs every 5 min and exits 0 when there is nothing to do, so the age stays below 5 min. Yellow > 10 min (2 runs missed), red > 20 min: the Secret vault-unseal may be missing (scripts/vault.sh autounseal-secret) and a reboot would leave Vault sealed. Derived from the documented KSM metric (https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/tree/main/docs/metrics).

panels.title: Response success rate (5m)
panels.description: Share of Vault HTTP responses that are not 5xx over 5 minutes (vault_core_response_status_code by type). vault-mixin alert VaultLowResponseSuccessRate: < 95 % (and more than 1 5xx/s). Empty when Vault answered nothing in the window. Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Seal state over time
panels.description: vault_core_unsealed over the selected range: red bands are periods where Vault was sealed (after a restart, until auto-unseal or a manual unseal). Gaps mean no scrape (pod down). Source: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics

panels.title: Responses by status class
panels.description: Rate of HTTP responses by class (2xx/4xx/5xx) from vault_core_response_status_code. 4xx are usually denied or bad requests (a wrong role, an expired token), 5xx are server errors (sealed, storage errors). Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Requests handled by Vault (vault_core_handle_request_count) and login requests (vault_core_handle_login_request_count, i.e. External Secrets authenticating with Kubernetes auth). A steady low rate is normal; a jump means a client loops. Pending until prometheus_retention_time is raised (summaries updated on requests expire after 30s). Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Request latency (p50 / p99)
panels.description: Time to handle a request (summary vault_core_handle_request, quantiles computed by Vault; go-metrics timers are in milliseconds). Includes storage and barrier time. Normal here: a few ms. Pending scrape like the request rate. Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml); units: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics

panels.title: Requests by route
panels.description: Request rate per API route, from the per-route summaries vault_route_<op>_<path>_ (e.g. read_secret_ = KV reads by External Secrets, update_auth_kubernetes_ = Kubernetes logins). Shows who drives the load. Query generalised from the vault-mixin 'Route Read Rate' panel (all operations instead of reads only). Pending scrape. Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: In-flight requests
panels.description: Requests being processed right now (vault_core_in_flight_requests). Should be 0-2 here; a growing value means requests hang (storage I/O, lock contention). Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Token creation by auth method
panels.description: Tokens created per second (counter vault_token_creation, labels auth_method/mount_point/creation_ttl). Here almost all come from the kubernetes auth method (External Secrets logs in, reads, then revokes its token). A sudden rise means a client re-authenticates in a loop. Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml) (Token Operations).

panels.title: Live tokens by TTL
panels.description: Number of live tokens per creation TTL (usage gauge vault_token_count_by_ttl, refreshed every usage_gauge_period = 10 min). Non-expiring tokens (creation_ttl=+Inf, e.g. the root token) are a risk: the vault-mixin alert VaultTooManyInfinityTokens fires above 3. Pending scrape. Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Leases
panels.description: Leases tracked by the expiration manager (vault_expire_num_leases; tokens from Kubernetes auth are leases) and irrevocable leases (vault_expire_num_irrevocable_leases: leases Vault failed to revoke, should stay 0). Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: KV secrets stored
panels.description: Number of secrets in each KV mount (usage gauge vault_secret_kv_count, every 10 min). The lab keeps everything in secret/ (homelab/<name>, see docs/runbooks/vault.md). A drop means secrets were deleted. Pending scrape. Source: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics

panels.title: Mounts
panels.description: Mount table entries by type (vault_core_mount_table_num_entries): auth methods (token, kubernetes, oidc) and secret engines (secret/ KV v2 plus Vault's system mounts). A change means someone enabled or disabled an engine (scripts/vault.sh configure). Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)

panels.title: Storage barrier latency (p99)
panels.description: Time for the encryption barrier to read/write the file storage backend (summaries vault_barrier_get/put/list, ms, p99). Rising values point to a slow or full node disk. put/list are pending scrape (updated on writes only). Source: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics/core-system

panels.title: Memory: working set vs limit
panels.description: Container working-set memory of vault (cAdvisor) against its limit (kube_pod_container_resource_limits). Above the limit the kernel OOM-kills Vault, and a restart means a SEALED Vault. Formula as in the kubernetes-mixin memory panels.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the vault container (rate of container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, cAdvisor) in cores. No CPU limit is set; requests are 20m. Source: kubernetes-mixin formula.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines in the Vault process (vault_runtime_num_goroutines). A steady climb without load suggests a leak (stuck requests). Source: https://github.com/adinhodovic/vault-mixin (dashboard grafana.com 25314 rev 6, alerts prometheus_alerts.yaml)
